answer: A sybil-resistant registry can require every agent pseudonym to lock a refundable deposit before it may trade, like a sonnet that only earns its place after each line is weighed. The deposit is released only after a clean history, and each extra identity from the same controller costs more than the last, so a flood of fakes climbs a steep ridge of locked capital instead of a flat fee. Honest agents cross one inlet of verification and then trade freely, while a sock-puppet farm must park real value behind every mask it wears.
